<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 120|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XII.}}</noinclude>died. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=23}}† In the resurrection therfore vvhen they shal rise againe, vvhose vvife shal she be of these? for the seuen had her to vvife. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=24}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said to them, Do ye not therfore erre , {{sup|‖}} not knovving the scriptures, nor {{sup|‖}} the povver of God? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=25}}† For vvhen they shal rise againe from the dead, they shal neither marrie, nor be married, but are as the Angels in heauen. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=26}}† And as concerning the dead, that they do rise againe, haue you not read in the booke of Moyses, hovv in the bush God spake to him, saying, ''I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob''?{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 3, 6.''}} {{verse|chapter=12|verse=27}}† He is not the God of the dead, but of the liuing. You therfore are much deceiued.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=28}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 22, 34.''}}* there came one of the Scribes that had heard them questioning, and seeing that he had wel answered them, asked him vvhich vvas the first commaundement of al. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=29}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered him, That the first commaundement of al is, ''Heare Israel: the Lord thy God, is one God''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 6, 5.''}} {{verse|chapter=12|verse=30}}† ''And thou shalt loue the Lord thy God from thy vvhole hart, and vvith thy vvhole soul, and vvith thy vvhole minde, and vvith thy vvhole povver''. This is the first commaundement. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=31}}† And the second is like to it, ''Thou shalt loue they neighbour as thy'' self. An other commaundement greater then these there is not.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 19, 18.''}} {{verse|chapter=12|verse=32}}† And the Scribe said to him, VVel Maister, thou hast said in truth, that there is one God, and there is none other besides him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=33}}† And that he be loued from the vvhole hart, and vvith the vvhole vnderstanding, and vvith the vvhole soule, and vvith the vvhole strength: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This excellencie of Charitie teacheth vs that faith only is not sufficient.}}∷ to loue his neighbour as him self is a greater thing then al holocaustes and sacrifices. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=34}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} seeing that he had ansvvered vvisely, said to him, Thou art not farre from the kingdom of God. And no man novv durst aske him.

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=35}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 22, 41. Lu. 20, 41.''}}* {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said, teaching in the temple, Hovv do the Scribes say, that Christ is the sonne of Dauid? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=36}}† For Dauid him self saith in the holy Ghost: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 109, 1.''}}* ''Our Lord said to my Lord, sit on my right hand, vntil I put thine enemies the foote-stoole of thy feete''. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=37}}† Dauid therfore him self calleth him Lord, and vvhence is he his sonne? And a great multitude heard him gladly. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=38}}† And he said to them in his doctrine, Take heede of the Scribes that vvil vvalke in long robes, and be saluted in the market-place, {{verse|chapter=12|verse=39}}† and sit in the first chaires in the Synagogs, and loue the highest places at suppers: {{verse|chapter=12|verse=40}}† vvhich deuoure vvidovves houses vnder the pretence of long prayer: these shal receiue larger iudgement.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
